Bokke: 2019 Rugby World Cup Champions

By: Julian Sun | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We celebrate the coronation of the Springboks as 2019 Rugby World Cup Champions

Unique Selling Point:
On Saturday, Siya Kolisi became the first black Springbok Captain to hold aloft the William Webb Ellis Trophy, as South Africa won the Rugby World Cup for the third time in their history. Just like in 1995 when Francois Pienaar was handed the trophy by a beaming Madiba, the country came together to celebrate the victory. At a time in which South Africa is desperate for good news, can the Boks' victory rekindle the spirit of the Rainbow Nation and unite the country once more?

Summary:
We celebrate the crowning of the Springboks as 2019 Rugby World Cup Champions. We look back on their momentous march to the final in Japan and celebrate a new generation of Springbok heroes, from Captain Siya Kolisi to the wonderful wings of Makazole Mapimpi & Cheslin Kolbe, to flyhalf Handre Pollard as well as the coach Rassie Erasmus.

We take in the scenes of the Boks' homecoming at OR Tambo and the open-top bus parade through Johannesburg, Pretoria & Soweto.

To provide context, we will also interview rugby journalists and past players .

Press Release:


The Return of the Champions
1995, 2007 and now 2019 - after a thrilling Rugby World Cup championship victory, the Springboks touched down in South Africa as national heroes and for at least a moment, united a divided country. But for a young boy from Zwide township in the Eastern Cape who would one day lift the coveted Webb Ellis Trophy in Japan, this was more than just a story book ending. Carte Blanche tracks the return of the champions.

Script:


SCRIPT
V/O: They say that lightning doesn’t strike twice… but then again South African rugby has always proved the exception to the rule…

It happened first, way back in 1995

Then again in 2007

And last Saturday, amazingly, history repeated itself once more.

On a crisp autumn evening in Yokahama, Japan, Siya Kolisi became only the third Springbok Captain to hold aloft the William Webb Ellis Trophy as South Africa were crowned winners of the 2019 Rugby World Cup.

The poignant image of the first Black Captain to lead the Boks to glory was seared indelibly into the collective memories of millions of South Africans.

At a time in which we are faced with so many challenges can this victory help unite the country and rekindle the spirit of the rainbow nation?



LINK: I’m here at the arrivals hall of OR Tambo amongst a legion of fans waiting to welcome the triumphant Springboks home. They return from Japan as World Champions carrying the greatest prize in rugby: The William Webb Ellis Trophy.


V/O: The cup is returning to local shores for the first time in 12 long years in the hands of a newly-minted South African hero.

Comment from Siya Kolisi at the Press Conference

V/O: It’s a far cry from 18 months ago when the Boks had fallen to 6th in the world, leading to the appointment of Rassie Erasmus as coach.

Rugby Journalist Sbu Mji-keliso recalls the monumental task needed to turn Bok fortunes around.

Comment from Sbu Mijikeliso



V/O: That man would be Siya Kolisi who became the first Black Captain to lead the Springboks at a World Cup

V/O: The Bok campaign got off to a shaky start when they lost their opening game to arch rivals New Zealand.

The defeat saw many write off the Boks chances. After all, no team has lost a pool match and gone on to win the tournament

But 2007 World Cup Winner Victor Matfield saw a silver lining.

Victor on the Boks getting an easier draw

V/O: The result was a string of victories taking them all the way to a semi-final against Wales which they won thanks to a Damian Der-lende try

Damian Da Allende on scoring the try v Wales


V/O: They would face favourites England in the final, fresh from a comprehensive thrashing of the All Blacks

Comment from Victor

V/O: The stage was set for one of the greatest performances in Springbok History.

Comments from Victor, Sbu and Springboks about final

V/O: Then midway through the second half, a moment of magic.

Mapimpi try

V/O: It was left to little Cheslin Kolbe to apply the coup de grace


And when the final whistle blew another amazing chapter in the annals of springbok rugby was written

As he raised the cup, Siya Kolisi was lifting more than just the World Cup trophy but also, the spirit of an entire nation.

Comments about the significance of Siya lifting the cup

V/O: Following the formalities, a night of revelry ensued

Beat about partying in the change room

V/O: As the Springboks returned home to a heroes welcome, an 18 month journey of redemption was complete


LINK I’m here at the Union buildings for the start of the Springboks valedictory bus parade. Winning the Rugby World Cup has led to an outpouring of national joy as citizens from all walks of life spill out onto the streets to celebrate their heroes.

Comments about what it means to South Africa to win the world cup and what it can do for the country.
